newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs flat,instance up $1-dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs flat,instance up $1-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Tuesday were mostly steady, with the exception of Illinois hogs, which were up $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.

Prices in Illinois were boosted by strong packer demand that offset increased marketings, with $57.00 to $57.50 paid in the country and $58.00 to $58.50 paid at plants. Some plants bid up to $60.00 for top quality hogs, dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota prices paid for hogs were steady with Monday at $57.00 to $57.50 in the country and $58.00 to $58.50 at plants, sources there said.

Indiana hog prices were steady at $57.00 to $57.50 in the country and up to $58.00 at plants, central Indiana dealers said. Marketings were light as producers were taking advantage of cool weather to let hogs put on more weight, one dealer said. Recent hot weather had slowed weight gains, he said.
Ohio hogs also sold steady at $55.00 to $55.50 in the country and $57.00 to $58.00 at plants.

Prices were underpinned by firm pork prices on Monday following light slaughter as several plants took plant holidays, the dealers said. Pork cut-out values rose $0.33 to $0.35 per cwt Monday, USDA said.
